summary.en: The CRPF has redeployed an anti-Naxal battalion from Chhattisgarh to Manipur and launched joint operations in Kulgam, while district commissioners are setting up social media cells after two security personnel were killed in Kishtwar. In Manipur, Naga and Kuki groups are clashing, with killings of Naga civilians on the Imphal-Ukhrul highway and a Kuki woman, prompting a bandh. In Kashmir, security forces conducted surprise night inspections at religious sites in Srinagar and arrested a person for spreading false information about the Kulgam attack. The UCDP recorded 437 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: CRPF har omplassert et anti-Naxal-bataljon fra Chhattisgarh til Manipur og igangsatt felles operasjoner i Kulgam, mens distriktskommissærer oppretter sosiale-medie-celler etter at to sikkerhetsansatte ble drept i Kishtwar. I Manipur er Naga‑ og Kuki-gruppene i konflikt, med drap på Naga-sivile på Imphal-Ukhrul-veien og en Kuki-kvinne, noe som har ført til en bandh. I Kashmir gjennomførte sikkerhetsstyrker overraskende nattlige inspeksjoner på religiøse steder i Srinagar og arresterte en person for å spre falsk informasjon om Kulgam-angrepet. UCDP registrerte 437 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
